correctness.rationale: The defining quantifiers of \(s(X)\) were reconstructed explicitly. Infinite-dimensional sigma-finite \(L_p\) spaces admit pairwise disjoint positive finite-measure supports, giving the universal lower bound \(2^{1/p}\). For \(1<p\le2\) the conjugate-exponent Clarkson inequality gives the matching upper bound. For \(p>2\), Clarkson gives the upper bound \(2^{1-1/p}\); atomlessness attains it for every unit vector by splitting the probability measure \(|x|^p d\mu\) in half and flipping the sign. If an atom is present, a unit vector supported on that atom reduces every competitor to a scalar parameter \(a\in[0,1]\), where \((1-a)^p+1-a^p\le2\). The endpoint \(p=1\) follows from the support lower bound and the diameter bound \(2\), and \(p=2\) is consistent from both branches.

value.rationale: The claim completes a natural exact computation for the numerical invariant \(s(X)\) on the basic \(L_p\) scale and reveals a sharp structural transition invisible to the qualitative LOH endpoint. For \(p>2\), one atom changes the exact value from \(2^{1-1/p}\) to \(2^{1/p}\); this is a mathematically motivated atomicity detector, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The formula unifies the previously listed Hilbert benchmark at \(p=2\) and the classical sequence-space behavior while identifying a genuinely different atomless regime.
